Governance.Principle: Contract-first GRACE changes establish ownership, invariants, verification and scope before source implementation.
Normative context, graph and verification projections are durable source of truth; explanatory documents cannot override them.
Semantic anchors remain stable, attribute-free tags for modules, data flows, graph documents and verification entries.
Approval, execution evidence, and applied lifecycle state are distinct. A planned or approved contract is not a passing test.

Architecture.Principle: Build one target architecture directly: shared Rust transfer contracts, Kotlin platform ownership, and Compose user interfaces on the named platforms.

Keep ownership singular. Kotlin owns Android lifecycle, permissions, network selection, and energy scheduling; Rust owns portable transfer correctness and the Windows receiver; UI consumes owner projections.
Prefer narrow versioned boundaries and explicit state over a second local source of truth or a broad aggregate bridge.
Do not add a permanent watch background daemon, a phone data relay, or temporary rewrite stages to solve a one-way transfer problem.

IntegrityAndRecovery.Principle: At-least-once network messages must converge to exactly-once durable file outcome through stable logical identity, idempotent requests, durable checkpoints, and atomic publication.
A receiver acknowledges only durable state that survives its documented crash boundary.
Corrupt, reordered, replayed, incomplete, or incompatible input fails closed without modifying the original recording.
Every recovery and cleanup path is cancellable, bounded, observable, and safe to repeat.

EnergyAndLifecycle.Principle: True idle is inactive: no persistent socket, Wi-Fi request, wake lock, filesystem polling, or perpetual discovery listener remains on the watch.
Discovery, retries, file reads, transfer sessions, and scheduled work have explicit deadlines and ceilings.
Release network, wake, callback, descriptor, coroutine, and subscription resources on success, cancellation, timeout, error, receiver loss, and thermal stop.
Energy behavior is measured on the target watch with matched controls; assumed battery or thermal results are not implementation guarantees.

SecurityAndPrivacy.Principle: Pairing is user-confirmed, revocable, identity-pinned, and separate from endpoint discovery.
Encrypted transport, replay defense, bounded resource admission, safe paths, and protected key storage are mandatory protocol properties.
Diagnostics minimize recording metadata and redact filenames unless explicit diagnostic mode is enabled.
Security review precedes selection of concrete cryptographic crates and pairing protocol details.

Evidence.Principle: Keep confirmed product decisions separate from unverified Samsung access, hotspot routing, network binding, and battery assumptions.
Use local tests for code contracts and physical tests for device, topology, file-access, thermal, and energy claims.
Never label an unexecuted gate passed and never infer third-party app access from ADB shell visibility.
When a requirement is unknown, preserve it as a named acceptance gate rather than inventing a guarantee.
